figures.title: Disruption rank and citations by team size
figures.caption: Larger teams generally rank lower on disruption and receive more citations, but neither pattern holds at every step. The panels show 7,933 works with a recorded reference and at least one later work citing them through 23 November 2026. On each work, at least one author listed Columbia University or an institution that OpenAlex lists under it. Panel A averages each work’s disruption percentile, its rank on a 0–100 scale among works from the same publication year. Higher ranks indicate greater disruption. The dashed line marks 50, the middle of the rank scale. Panel B shows the median number of distinct later works citing each work. Works less likely to be sampled count more. The counts below the equally spaced team sizes are the actual numbers of works. The dotted line separates individual sizes from size ranges. For the 477 works by teams of 51–100 authors, the median is 39 citing works, with a 95% confidence interval from 31 to 46 [T66]. Each bar gives a 95% confidence interval for one estimate. The intervals come from recalculating the estimates and ranks in 1,000 repeated draws within every original team-size group, including the largest. The same work could be drawn more than once in each repetition. Compare with Figure 2 of the original study [brief].

issues.problem: The caption explains how to read a disruption percentile but not what makes a work rank as more disruptive. It also leaves the set of works used for the same-year comparison implicit.
issues.fix: Add a short explanation that a work scores as more disruptive when later works tend to cite it without also citing the works it referenced. Name the set of works used to calculate the ranks within each year.

issues.problem: The caption explains how the uncertainty bars were calculated but does not say that the largest team-size group was fully sampled.
issues.fix: State that the data include every eligible work in the 51–100 author group and that its bars still show how much the estimate varied across repeated draws from those works.

figures.title: Disruption rank by team size in fields with enough data
figures.caption: Larger teams had lower estimated disruption ranks in 14 of the 20 fields and 24 of the 34 subfields that met the sample requirements. Many field intervals include zero. Only one journal met the requirements, so the result for most journals could not be tested. The field and subfield pattern was partly reproduced [T69, T70]. The dots show the estimated difference in disruption rank across works for a doubling of the number of authors. The dashed line marks no estimated difference. The score compares later works that cite the work without any of its references with those that cite both. Later works that cite only the references also count toward the total used to scale the score. The percentile is the rank of that score among works published in the same year. Works with 1–10 authors had a recorded reference and at least one later work citing them through 23 November 2026. Each had at least one author listing Columbia University or an institution that OpenAlex lists under it. Works less likely to be sampled count more in the estimates. Parentheses show actual work counts. To be included, a field, subfield or journal needed at least 30 works, at least 5 in each of the 1–2 and 5–10 author ranges, and at least 4 distinct team sizes. The second table column counts groups that met those requirements out of all groups seen in the sample. Each bar gives a 95% confidence interval for one field’s estimate. Each table range gives a 95% interval for the percentage of eligible groups with estimates below zero. The intervals come from 1,000 repeated draws within each original team-size group, including the largest, allowing repeats and recalculating ranks. The table gives each eligible group equal weight and keeps the same groups in each draw. Compare with the field comparisons in Figure 3 and Extended Data of the original study [brief].

issues.problem: The displayed title says “Disruption,” but the figure plots differences in disruption rank, not in the score itself. The axis phrase “per author doubling” is also compressed.
issues.fix: Use the same title in the image and caption, and name the rank in both. Label the axis “Difference in disruption rank when team size doubles (percentile points).”

issues.problem: The caption describes which citations count but does not explain what makes a score higher or how to read an interval that crosses zero.
issues.fix: Say that the score is higher when more later papers cite the paper without citing its references than cite both. Explain that a bar crossing zero means the data do not clearly show whether the rank is lower or higher for larger teams.

issues.problem: The phrase “including the largest” could mean the group with the most papers or the group with the largest teams. The relevant detail is that the resampling also included the group whose papers were all sampled.
issues.fix: Omit that phrase from the caption and, if needed, explain in the methods appendix that the repeated draws also included the team-size group for which every paper was sampled.

figures.title: Reference ages and citation counts in three team-size groups
figures.caption:
Both larger groups cite newer and generally more highly cited references than solo authors do. The two larger groups have similar citation-count curves. A lower curve in panel A means fewer references older than the age shown. A higher curve in panel B means more references above the citation count shown.

The works had at least one later work citing them through 23 November 2026. Each had at least one author listing Columbia University or an institution that OpenAlex lists under it. The curves pool the available reference links, counting each reference once per work that lists it. Each link carries that work’s weight, so works less likely to be sampled count more per link, and works with more links contribute more. In order of 1, 10 and 51–100 authors, both panels use 597, 624 and 477 works. Panel A uses 22,001, 34,531 and 43,548 links; panel B uses 22,149, 34,613 and 43,772 [T75]. Reference age is the difference in publication years. Panel A includes same-year references, excludes references published in later years and shows ages through 100 years. Panel B uses current citation totals, not totals at publication. Its scale is linear through one citation and logarithmic above one.

Shading shows sampling uncertainty at each age or citation-count cutoff, not for the curve as a whole. Each 95% confidence interval comes from 1,000 repeated draws within every original team-size group, including the group with the largest teams. A work could be picked more than once per draw.

The figure supports the observed comparison in these three groups, not the full finding about fitted distributions. In separate fits, older references became less common faster for ten-author works than for solo works. The fitted comparison among references with 50 or more citations was inconclusive [T76, T77]. Compare with Figure 4 of the original study [brief].

issues.problem: C5 says that the fitted patterns for both reference age and citation counts vary with team size. The figure shows observed curves for three groups, not fitted curves. The separate model results support an age difference between ten-author and solo works, but the comparison for references with at least 50 citations is inconclusive.
issues.fix: Revise C5 to say that, in this sample, works with 10 or 51–100 authors cited newer and generally more highly cited references than solo works did. Report the model results separately and mark the original finding as partly reproduced. Keep the plotted data and marks unchanged.

issues.problem: The caption uses “separate fits” and “fitted comparison” without explaining those terms.
issues.fix: Say that separate statistical models, not shown here, estimated how quickly older references become less common and compared citation counts among references with at least 50 citations.

figures.title: Disruption rank by team size and citation rank
figures.caption:
The original citation comparison was partly reproduced. Disruption rank fell as team size increased in the least-cited half. The data do not establish a decline in the other citation groups or a steeper decline in the most-cited tenth.

Each point shows the mean disruption percentile for one team-size and citation group. Each bar gives a separate 95% confidence interval for that average, not for a change with team size. The figure covers 7,933 works with a recorded reference and at least one later work citing them through 23 November 2026. Each work had an author listing Columbia University or an institution that OpenAlex lists under it. The disruption score compares later works that cite a work without any of its references with those that cite both. Higher disruption ranks mean greater disruption relative to works published in the same year. Citation rank compares counts of distinct later citing works among works from that same year. The middle group starts at the 50th percentile and stops just before the 90th. The legend gives actual work counts. Works less likely to be sampled count more. The intervals come from recalculating both kinds of rank and the citation groups in 1,000 repeated draws within every original team-size group, including the largest, allowing a work to be picked more than once. The dashed line marks the middle of the disruption rank scale. The dotted line separates individual team sizes from ranges. The ranges above ten authors are shown for comparison only.

The estimates of change use teams with 1–10 authors. For each doubling of team size, the rank in the lowest citation group fell by an estimated 2.50 percentile points, with a 95% interval from a fall of 3.39 to a fall of 1.64, based on 3,277 works. In the middle group, the estimate was a fall of 1.22 points, with a 95% interval from a fall of 2.54 to a rise of 0.48, based on 2,476 works. In the top tenth, the estimate was a rise of 0.23 points, with a 95% interval from a fall of 4.33 to a rise of 3.37, based on 457 works. The estimated change was 2.73 points higher in the top tenth than in the lowest half, with a 95% interval from 1.89 points lower to 6.00 points higher, based on 3,734 works [T68]. Compare with the citation comparison in Figure 3 of the original study [brief].

issues.problem: The figure is listed as supporting C3, but it supports only part of that claim. Disruption rank declined with team size in the least-cited half. The intervals do not establish a decline in the other citation groups or a steeper decline in the most-cited tenth.
issues.fix: Keep the plot and estimates unchanged. In the report, present C3 as the original finding being tested, and mark it as partly reproduced. Use the caption's qualified conclusion when citing this figure.

issues.problem: The caption gives the number of works in each citation group and says that some works count more, but it does not make clear that this also affects which group a work belongs to. Readers may wonder why the lowest half contains fewer than half of the plotted works.
issues.fix: Say that works less likely to be sampled count more both when setting the citation groups and when calculating the plotted averages. Clarify that the legend counts each sampled work once.

figures.title: Distributions of disruption scores by team size
figures.caption: Most scores are close to zero. Just left of zero, the curves show that larger teams have a greater share of works with negative scores. Each curve shows the percentage of works at or below the score on the horizontal axis. The jump at zero counts only works with a score of exactly zero. The curves cover 600 solo works, 624 works by ten authors and 477 works by teams of 51–100 authors [T67]. All had a recorded reference and at least one later work citing them through 23 November 2026. On each work, at least one author listed Columbia University or an institution that OpenAlex lists under it. Works less likely to be sampled count more. A score is positive when more later works cite the work without citing any of its references than cite both the work and its references. A negative score means the reverse. Later works that cite the references but not the work also count toward the total used to scale the score [brief]. The plot shows scores from negative 0.1 to positive 0.1 and spreads out values near zero. Shading shows the uncertainty in the estimated percentage at each score separately, not for the whole curve at once. These 95% confidence intervals come from 1,000 repeated draws within each original team-size group, including the largest. A work could be picked more than once per draw. This is not a panel-for-panel redraw of the original study. Its closest comparison is the Extended Data analysis of differences in the full disruption-score distributions across team sizes [brief].

issues.problem: The caption refers to the original study’s Extended Data analysis but does not identify a specific figure or panel.
issues.fix: If [brief] identifies the closest figure or panel, give its number in the caption and keep the note that this is not a direct redraw. If there is no matching panel, say so explicitly.

method: Only text was changed after the original layout pass. The original plot routines rerendered all five originals pixel for pixel. PDF at 150 dpi and native 250 dpi PNG comparisons after hiding the text were also pixel-exact for every original and redraw. Axes, crop, marks, legend keys and displayed numbers were unchanged. No analyses or API calls.
script:
# Figure-only wording update. Run with the harness load() helper from the workspace.
# Uses the released plotting routines and saved estimates; never runs the analysis.
from pathlib import Path
import io, json, re, hashlib, shutil, subprocess, tempfile, copy
from matplotlib.text import Text
from matplotlib.legend import Legend
from matplotlib.offsetbox import TextArea
from matplotlib.table import Table
from matplotlib.ticker import FuncFormatter
from PIL import Image
import numpy as np

parents = {'fig2-team-stage2':'P15', 'fig3-fields-stage2':'P16', 'fig4-empirical-stage2':'P17',
           'fig3-impact-stage2':'P18', 'ext-raw-disruption-stage2':'P19'}
slugs = {'P15':'team-size-and-disruption', 'P16':'disruption-by-field', 'P17':'references-by-team-size',
         'P18':'disruption-by-citation-rank', 'P19':'disruption-score-distributions'}
original_paths = {f['id']: f['immutable_gate_files'] for f in load('J14')['figures']}
words = {
'P15': {'Mean D percentile (0–100)':'Mean disruption percentile (0–100)',
        'Median citing works (count)':'Median number of citing works',
        'A  Disruption rank':'A  Disruption rank by team size', 'B  Citation count':'B  Citations by team size',
        'Team size (authors; sample n below each size band)':'Team size (authors), with number of works below'},
'P16': {'Change in mean D percentile per doubling of authors (points)':'Rank difference per author doubling (percentile points)',
        '20 supported OpenAlex fields • teams of 1–10 authors':'Disruption by team size in 20 fields (1–10 authors)',
        'Grouping':'Group type', 'Supported /\nobserved':'Enough data /\nseen in sample',
        'Negative\nslopes':'Lower rank for\nlarger teams\n(estimated)', '95% bootstrap\ninterval':'95% confidence\ninterval'},
'P17': {'A  Reference age':'A  Age of cited references', 'B  Reference popularity':'B  Citations to those references',
        'Current reference citations (count; symlog)':'Current citations per reference (count)',
        'Weighted share of edges above threshold':'References above the value shown (%)'},
'P18': {'Mean D percentile (0–100)':'Mean disruption percentile (0–100)',
        'Within-year citation impact (unweighted n)':'Disruption rank by team size and citation rank',
        'Bottom 50% (n=3,768)':'Lowest half (3,768)',
        '50th–<90th (n=3,278)':'Middle ranks (3,278)',
        '90th–100th (n=887)':'Top tenth (887)'},
'P19': {'Raw disruption score D (symmetric log scale)':'Disruption score (negative: development; positive: disruption)',
        'Works at or below D (%)':'Works at or below score (%)'},
}

def new_word(parent, text):
    if text in words[parent]: return words[parent][text]
    if parent == 'P16': return re.sub(r' \(n=([0-9,]+)\)$', r' (\1)', text)
    if parent == 'P19': return re.sub(r' \(n=([0-9,]+)\)$', r' (\1)', text)
    return text

def pixels(raw):
    return np.asarray(Image.open(io.BytesIO(raw)).convert('RGB'))

def render_pdf(raw):
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as folder:
        p = Path(folder)/'panel.pdf'; p.write_bytes(raw)
        return subprocess.run(['pdftoppm','-singlefile','-r','150','-png',str(p)],capture_output=True,check=True).stdout

def sha(raw): return hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()

parity = {}
def write_words(fig, original_slug):
    parent=parents[original_slug]; slug=slugs[parent]; evidence={}
    for ext, original_file in zip(('pdf','png'),original_paths[parent]):
        def render(mode):
            model=copy.deepcopy(fig)
            if ext=='png':
                model.savefig(io.BytesIO(),format='pdf',dpi=250,bbox_inches='tight',facecolor='white')
            get_bbox=model.get_tightbbox
            positions=[]; edits=[]; outside=[]; undo=[]
            def crop(renderer, *args, **kwargs):
                # This runs after the original layout pass. Use the original crop and do not rerun layout.
                bbox=get_bbox(renderer,*args,**kwargs)
                positions.extend([list(ax.get_position().bounds) for ax in model.axes])
                positions.append(list(bbox.bounds))
                if mode.startswith('words'):
                    # Preserve legend keys, frames and text anchors by retaining the original text boxes.
                    for legend in model.findobj(Legend):
                        for area in legend._legend_box.findobj(TextArea):
                            fixed=area.get_bbox(renderer)
                            area.get_bbox=lambda renderer, fixed=fixed: fixed
                    for ax in model.axes:
                        formatter=ax.yaxis.get_major_formatter()
                        if parent=='P16' and isinstance(formatter,FuncFormatter):
                            formatter.func = lambda x, pos, original=formatter.func: new_word(parent, original(x,pos))
                    table_labels=[cell.get_text() for table in model.findobj(Table) for cell in table.get_celld().values()]
                    for artist in model.findobj(Text)+table_labels:
                        old=artist.get_text(); new=new_word(parent,old)
                        if new==old: continue
                        edits.append([old,new]); undo.append((artist,old)); anchor=artist.get_position()
                        artist.set_text(new); assert artist.get_position()==anchor
                        box=artist.get_window_extent(renderer).transformed(model.dpi_scale_trans.inverted())
                        if box.x0 < bbox.x0-.099 or box.x1 > bbox.x1+.099 or box.y0 < bbox.y0-.099 or box.y1 > bbox.y1+.099:
                            outside.append((new,list(box.bounds)))
                if mode.endswith('-hidden'):
                    for artist in model.findobj(Text)+[cell.get_text() for table in model.findobj(Table) for cell in table.get_celld().values()]: artist.set_alpha(0)
                return bbox
            model.get_tightbbox=crop
            try:
                b=io.BytesIO(); model.savefig(b,format=ext,dpi=250,bbox_inches='tight',facecolor='white'); raw=b.getvalue()
            finally:
                del model.get_tightbbox
                for artist,old in undo: artist.set_text(old)
            return raw,positions,edits,outside
        baseline, oldpos, _, _=render('original'); updated, newpos, edits, outside=render('words')
        orig=Path(original_file).read_bytes()
        # Original and amended renders use exactly the same axes and crop to floating-point precision.
        assert np.allclose(oldpos,newpos,rtol=0,atol=1e-10),parent
        if ext=='png': reference, reproduced, final=map(pixels,(orig,baseline,updated))
        elif shutil.which('pdftoppm'): reference, reproduced, final=(pixels(render_pdf(x)) for x in (orig,baseline,updated))
        else: reference=reproduced=final=None
        if reference is not None:
            assert reference.shape == reproduced.shape == final.shape, (parent,ext,reference.shape,reproduced.shape,final.shape)
            baseline_equal=bool(np.array_equal(reference,reproduced))
            assert baseline_equal, (parent,ext,int(np.count_nonzero(np.any(reference!=reproduced,axis=2))))
            changed_pixels=int(np.count_nonzero(np.any(reference!=final,axis=2)))
            stripped=[render(m)[0] for m in ('original-hidden','words-hidden')]
            if ext=='pdf': stripped=[render_pdf(x) for x in stripped]
            marks_exact=bool(np.array_equal(*map(pixels,stripped)))
            assert marks_exact,(parent,ext,'non-text pixels changed')
        else: baseline_equal=changed_pixels=marks_exact=None
        assert not outside, (parent,ext,outside)
        Path(f'figures/{slug}.{ext}').write_bytes(updated)
        evidence[ext]=dict(original_file=original_file,original_sha256=sha(orig),output_sha256=sha(updated),
            original_rerender_pixel_exact=baseline_equal,non_text_pixels_exact=marks_exact,changed_pixels=changed_pixels,axis_and_crop_bounds=newpos,
            changed_text=edits,changed_labels_outside_page=outside)
    parity[parent]=evidence

def render_relabels():
    ns={'load':load,'STAGE2_RUN':False}
    source=load('J15')['scripts']['analysis_stage2.py']
    exec(source.replace('    exec(figcode,ns)','    ns[\"write_words\"]=write_words; exec(figcode,ns)').replace(' exec(figcode,ns)',' ns[\"write_words\"]=write_words; exec(figcode,ns)'),ns)
    code=ns['figcode']; start=code.index('def save('); end=code.index('def err(',start)
    ns['figcode']=code[:start]+"def save(fig,slug):\n write_words(fig,slug)\n plt.close(fig)\n"+code[end:]
    ns['render_saved_stage2'].__globals__['write_words']=write_words
    ns['render_saved_stage2']()
    return parity

if __name__ == '__main__':
    print(json.dumps(render_relabels(),ensure_ascii=False,indent=2))
